Subject: Eval setup & recommended models - FinCorp (post-call recap)

Hi Samir / Priya -

Great to meet earlier - thanks for walking through the FinCorp use case (customer support summarization + routing). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get customer-specific evals running on Redwood: 

1) Recommended models to start: redwood-1.3-16k (base) and redwood-2-small-quant (intended for cost-sensitive low-latency) - we recommend A/Bing both for the first run to surface quality/cost tradeoffs.

2) Benchmarks & prompt sets: attached is a sample eval dataset (fincorp_eval_dataset_sample.csv) and the prompt_set_v1.md we discussed. Our public benchmark pack (see attached PDF) contains baseline numbers for comparable enterprise datasets.

3) Dataset format & upload: please provide a CSV with columns: id, prompt, expected_response, category (optional), and sensitivity_flag (Y/N). For private data, you can either upload to our secure S3 bucket (we'll share a pre-signed URL) or send via your secure file transfer. See the sample attached for formatting.

4) Scoring criteria we propose: a blended automated + human approach:
   - Primary automated metrics: BLEU/ROUGE for extractive match, BERTScore for semantic similarity, and an exact-match rate for routing labels.
   - Thresholds: we typically flag regressions >5% drop vs baseline on BERTScore or >7% increase in routing error rate.
   - Human judgment: 1000-sample human spot checks on high-impact categories (fraud, compliance).

5) How Redwood runs customer evals: once dataset is uploaded we create a dedicated eval job in your staging project, run against recommended model variants with consistent seeding and temperature settings (we lock sampling to deterministic where possible), and produce per-prompt scores + aggregated report. We also surface token-level cost estimates.

6) Next steps (proposed):
   - You: share final eval dataset (or give us S3 access) and confirm target categories + any redline-sensitive prompts (by Thu 11/19).
   - Us (Redwood): spin up staging eval job, run baseline models, and deliver a results deck + open issues list within 48 business hours of dataset receipt.

I've cc'd Dylan (solutions) to help with access; Neha (applied ML) will chime in with scoring details below.

Thanks - happy to hop back on a 20-min call if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales 
Redwood Inference

Hi Samir / Priya - quick technical follow-up from the applied ML side: happy to run the eval and here's the detail you asked for.

1) BERTScore: we use the original BERTScore implementation with multilingual models (v0.3.11) and report both precision/recall/F1 at the sentence level. For longer passages we chunk to sentence-level and report macro-aggregated scores. If you prefer an aggregated-passage metric instead we can provide that as an alternative column.

2) Other automated metrics: we run ROUGE-L and chrF for extractive-style checks and a routing-label exact-match for classification tasks. We also compute length/entropy diagnostics to catch degenerate outputs.

3) Thresholds & regression detection: our default alerting is set to detect regressions >5% absolute on BERTScore-F1 or >7% absolute increase in routing label error. We can tune these thresholds for FinCorp categories - for any category you mark as high-impact (fraud / compliance) we'll run additional human evaluation sampling.

4) Data handling & retention: for evals uploaded to our staging S3 we keep data for 30 days by default and then purge; if you require different retention we can set a shorter window or perform immediate purge after run. All data in staging is encrypted at rest (KMS) and access is restricted to the eval job. We will send the S3 pre-signed link & upload instructions to Samir and security@fincorp.com separately.

5) Eval job config (what we'll run):
   - Models: redwood-1.3-16k (deterministic sampling), redwood-2-small-quant (temperature=0.0 for routing tasks; temp=0.7 for summarization A/B)
   - Seeds: fixed seed across runs for stochastic models; where determinism isn't possible we run 3 replicates and report mean/std.
   - Output: per-prompt scores (BERTScore, ROUGE-L, chrF), routing confusion matrix, token cost estimate, and an issues list with representative failing prompts.

6) Time estimates: once we have the dataset and S3 receipt confirmation, the baseline run for ~10k prompts usually completes within 48 business hours (i.e., 2 working days). We'll prioritize FinCorp queue for this POC.

7) Deliverables: a results deck (PDF), raw per-prompt CSV with scores, and a short recording/walkthrough.

If that looks good I'll proceed to create the staging job; Samir, if you share the S3 upload by Thu 11/19 we'll target initial results by Tue 11/23 COB.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
